distribution.summary: Chongqing; Fujian; Guangdong; Guangxi; Guizhou; Hainan; Sichuan; Xizang; Yunnan; Hong Kong; Taiwan
distribution.narrative: Yin et al. (1984) and Huang & Lu (2015) support Taiwan, Guangdong, Sichuan, Yunnan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangxi and Xizang. Smith et al. (2020) adds Chongqing, Guizhou and Hong Kong while confirming Yunnan and Taiwan. Beaver & Liu (2010) independently supports Taiwan; current promoted distribution remains unchanged. Lau (2025), Checklist of Insects of Hong Kong, 2nd edition, provides additional secondary checklist evidence for Hong Kong occurrence.

host_note: Baseline species-level host records and Smith et al. (2020) genus-level evidence are retained. Beaver & Liu (2010) explicitly records Camellia thea and Brownea sp. in Taiwan. The source wording Camellia thea is retained in evidence and not duplicated as a separate current host because the current synthesis already contains Camellia sinensis; Brownea sp. is added at source-supported genus resolution.
taxonomy_summary: The current accepted identity is Euwallacea fornicatus (Eichhoff, 1868).
